key_findings: **VBTABLE HYPOTHESIS DEFINITIVELY FALSIFIED**. CharaBase CHD attributes = 0x00000000. Bit 0x02 (CHD_VIRTINH = virtual inheritance) is NOT set. The +0x1bc and +0x220 fields are NOT vbptrs (virtual base pointers). MSVC virtual inheritance would require this bit to be set, plus a vbtable in .rdata containing virtual base offsets.

**OWNER-CLASS MISATTRIBUTION CORRECTED**: the +0x1bc and +0x220 fields are in **CharaBase-family instances** (CharaBase + PlayerBase + NpcBase + MyPlayer - the 50-slot vftable `Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::*` chara/actor classes), NOT in LTC/LGTC family instances. Evidence: LTC/LGTC instances allocate at most 0x78 (120) bytes (per Global's clone factory BCS-Y-1544), making +0x1bc (444 bytes) and +0x220 (544 bytes) far out-of-bounds. CharaBase methods (like slot 5 _onFinalize FUN_006FA7E0 -> firer FUN_006F6900) call FUN_00CC7510 with `this` = CharaBase instance, confirming CharaBase has these fields.

**CharaBase RTTI structure** (NEW catalog): vftable [[Control::CharaBase::vftable]] (BCS-Y-0184) at 0x00FD5CAC. Primary COL [[Application_Lua_Script_Client_Control_CharaBase_RTTI_Complete_Object_Locator]] (BCS-Y-1724 NEW) at 0x0115EC78. TD [[Application_Lua_Script_Client_Control_CharaBase_TypeDescriptor]] (BCS-Y-1721 NEW) at 0x012709A4. CHD [[Application_Lua_Script_Client_Control_CharaBase_ClassHierarchyDescriptor]] (BCS-Y-1722 NEW) at 0x0115EC8C with attributes=0x00, numBaseClasses=7. BCA [[Application_Lua_Script_Client_Control_CharaBase_BaseClassArray]] (BCS-Y-1723 NEW) at 0x0115EC9C with 7 BCDs (deferred enumeration).

**CharaBase uses NON-virtual SINGLE inheritance with 7 base classes** (CHD attr=0x00, numBaseClasses=7). Unlike the LTC/LGTC family which uses MI (CHD attr=0x01 or 0x05) with 11-15 BCDs, CharaBase has a LINEAR 7-level inheritance chain. Likely chain: CharaBase < ActorBase < LuaControl < LuaObject < LgeBase (or similar) - 7 levels deep. This is a different inheritance model than the LTC/LGTC family, despite sharing the `Control::*` namespace.

**THE 6 ADJACENT VFTABLES BEFORE CharaBase'S PRIMARY ARE STANDALONE CLASSES** (per the standalone-class neighbor pattern). The 6 vftables at 0x00FD5C28/2C/34/68/84/A0 each have their own primary COL (all with offset=0) and distinct TDs (0x012C2150, 0x012C2208, 0x012C22C0, 0x012C2348, 0x012C2388, 0x012C0F38). They are NOT CharaBase MI subobjects - they are independent classes that happen to be placed in adjacent .rdata. Likely typed-delegate/EventHandler<CharaBase,...> instantiations or similar template specializations.

**ALTERNATIVE WRITER HYPOTHESES** (post-vbtable falsification): the +0x1bc and +0x220 fields must be set by ONE of these mechanisms - (a) **LEA + setter-function pattern** (the FindOffsetWriters scan only detected `MOV [reg+0x1bc], val` displacement-encoded writes; it would miss `LEA EAX, [ECX+0x1bc]; PUSH EAX; CALL setter_fn` where the setter writes via *this offset 0); (b) **POST-FACTORY CLASS-REGISTRY BINDING** (CharaBaseClass is registered with class ID 16 in the identified LuaClassRegistry FUN_0078E3A0 BCS-Y-0398; the registry may set instance.+0x1bc to point to the per-class metadata entry when an instance is created); (c) **MEMCPY/MEMSET BLOCK INIT** from a class template in .rdata. Most likely (b) given the class-registry mechanism's existence and the +0x1bc reader's use of `*(this+0x1bc)` as a class-identity lookup.

**ARCHITECTURAL IMPLICATION FOR LUA-BRIDGE DISPATCH**: the LuaCallbackDispatcher (BCS-Y-0399 FUN_00CC7A90) and its 23 caller-cluster sister functions all read this+0x1bc via FUN_00CD7A30 (BCS-Y-1581) to identify the calling class for dispatch routing. Since `this` in these calls is a CharaBase-family instance (not LTC/LGTC), the dispatch model is: 'CharaBase-family object has a pointer to its registered class metadata at +0x1bc; the dispatcher reads this metadata to route the Lua callback to the right class-specific handler'. The LTC/LGTC family has a SEPARATE dispatch model (they have triple/dual allocator scopes and their dispatch uses vftable-based MI, not +0x1bc-based class-ID routing).
